title: The Singapore-Flagged Evergreen Ever Lovely Was Hit by a Projectile on the New IMO-Oman Southern Corridor at 2:10 p.m. UTC on 25 June. The WSJ Attributed It to the IRGC. The IMO Suspended Its 11,000-Seafarer Evacuation Within Hours. Iran's Strait Authority Said Off-Route Vessels 'Carry the Consequences.' The Corridor the US Helped Broker Is the Corridor Iran Just Shot At.
narrative:
On Wednesday June 24 and Thursday June 25 2026, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei escalated Tehran's response to the US-Iran memorandum of understanding signed June 18 by Trump and Pezeshkian. In an X post and weekly briefing, Baqaei accused US officials of making 'contradictory statements' that deepen Iranian 'historical mistrust,' invoked 'commitment for commitment,' and warned Washington against interpretations that 'contradict the explicit text' of the MoU. The trigger sequence: (1) Trump told reporters June 24 that Iran made 'very big concessions' and released Iranian funds would buy American agricultural goods and medicine; (2) Truth Social framed the same money as already-frozen assets under US supervision, not new money; (3) Trump separately claimed Tehran assured Washington 'no tolls, no insurance costs, and no other charges of any kind' in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran rejected each: Central Bank Governor Hemmati rejected the spending-mechanism framing; UN ambassador Bahreini rejected US pre-conditions on asset use; the Persian Gulf Strait Authority warned vessels outside Iran-designated routes would not be covered by safety, insurance, or liability protections.

The physical-evidence counter arrived hours later on June 25 in Hormuz. UKMTO reported at 2:10 p.m. UTC that the Singapore-flagged 9,532-TEU Evergreen containership Ever Lovely was struck by an unknown projectile on its starboard side approximately 7.5 nautical miles SE of Dahit, Oman, sustaining bridge damage, after completing a transit on the new IMO-Oman southern corridor with two sister ships (Ever Lotus, Ever Unicorn). The Wall Street Journal, citing two senior US officials, attributed the strike to Iran's IRGC. Windward tracked five tankers (Blue Star I, Azumasan, Omega Trader, Stoic Warrior, plus one vessel that went dark) reversing course after IRGC radio warnings: 'Transit only with IRGC permission, on designated routes. No permission, AIS off, or off-route, and you carry the consequences.' The IMO suspended its 11,000-seafarer evacuation operation hours after the strike; Secretary-General Dominguez said the Ever Lovely 'was not operating under the evacuation framework the IMO had established.' Iran had refused to join the IMO-Oman framework, calling it 'unacceptable and completely dangerous.' Brent ticked above $75/barrel. Follow-up US-Iran working-level talks are scheduled in Switzerland June 29-30.

analysis:
The Ever Lovely projectile strike at 2:10 p.m. UTC on June 25 is the first physical-evidence test of the June 18 US-Iran MOU's operative safe-passage regime on the IMO-Oman southern corridor. The US framing positions the MOU as Iran having agreed to (a) 'infinity' nuclear inspections, (b) no Hormuz tolls, (c) US-controlled release of frozen assets for American goods. The Iran framing positions the MOU as text-bound: (a) downblending of enriched uranium under IAEA supervision at sites not bombed last June, (b) no new nuclear weapons, (c) 'commitment for commitment' reciprocity. The Ever Lovely strike is the first test of which framing is operative on the water.

The structural finding is the IMO's action. Within hours of the strike, IMO Secretary-General Dominguez issued a statement that the Ever Lovely 'was not operating under the evacuation framework the IMO had established' and suspended the 11,000-seafarer evacuation launched the day before. The IMO's framework is the IMO-Oman southern corridor — the route the US helped broker, the route the Ever Lovely had just completed, the route Iran had refused to join, calling it 'unacceptable and completely dangerous.' The IMO's suspension is the first on-record institutional consequence of the strike: an evacuation plan designed to keep commercial traffic moving through the corridor was suspended because the strike demonstrated that the corridor is not safe in the way the framework assumed.

The IRGC radio broadcast recorded by Windward — 'Transit only with IRGC permission, on designated routes. No permission, AIS off, or off-route, and you carry the consequences' — is the first on-record IRGC threat-of-force formulation on the IMO-Oman corridor. The five tankers that reversed course (Blue Star I, Azumasan, Omega Trader, Stoic Warrior) plus the one vessel that went dark are the first commercial-vessel compliance pattern with the Iran-designated routes regime. The 70 crossings recorded earlier on the Oman route on June 25 — before the strike — are the volume metric for the corridor the US helped broker; the post-strike vessel behavior is the volume metric for the corridor Iran controls.

The WSJ attribution — 'two senior US officials' told the WSJ the IRGC attacked the Ever Lovely — is the first on-record US attribution of a Hormuz strike to the IRGC. The attribution is anonymous; the US intelligence community has not issued a public statement, and Iran's government has neither confirmed nor denied the strike. The asymmetry between the on-record anonymous US attribution and the absent on-record Iranian response is itself a structural finding: the strike is on the record as having happened (UKMTO advisory, Windward tracking, 70 crossings baseline, five tankers reversing) and on the record as attributed to the IRGC (WSJ sourcing), but the Iranian government has chosen neither to confirm nor to deny.

The three-day sequence — Trump rally June 24 'very big concessions' / Truth Social 'already-frozen assets under US supervision' / Trump 'no tolls, no insurance costs' on Hormuz; Baqaei 'contradictory statements' / Hemmati rejection / Strait Authority warning / IRGC 'consequences' broadcast; Ever Lovely strike / IMO suspension / 70 crossings → five tankers reversing — is the load-bearing structural finding. The US 'very big concessions' framing was issued on the same day as the three Iranian rejections, and the Iranian physical-evidence response arrived within 24 hours of Trump's Hormuz statement. The IMO's institutional action (suspension of the evacuation) is the strongest on-record signal to date that Iran's framing is the operative one on the corridor Iran did not authorize.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Six days after the June 18 Islamabad MOU signing, the Ever Lovely projectile strike at 7.5 nm SE of Dahit on the IMO-Oman southern corridor at 2:10 p.m. UTC on 25 June is the first physical-evidence test of the MOU's operative safe-passage regime. The WSJ attributed the strike to the IRGC via two senior US officials; the IMO suspended its 11,000-seafarer evacuation plan within hours; the IRGC 'Transit only with IRGC permission... you carry the consequences' radio broadcast was recorded by Windward alongside five tankers reversing course (Blue Star I, Azumasan, Omega Trader, Stoic Warrior). The structural finding: the corridor the US helped broker is the corridor Iran just shot at, and the 70 crossings recorded on the day of the strike were the first real test of whether Iran's safe-passage regime or international-law freedom of navigation applies. The IMO's institutional action — suspending the evacuation plan designed to keep commercial traffic moving through the corridor — is the strongest on-record evidence to date that Iran's framing is the operative one on the corridor Iran did not authorize. Beat-distinct from the June 22 Kpler/CENTCOM/Tasnim ship-count baseline (no projectile strike, no IMO suspension); from the June 23 Burgenstock 'infinity inspections' Day-1 framing (no Hormuz physical-event component); and from the June 24 Muscat Oman-Iran joint statement (political/diplomatic Hormuz framing, no physical-evidence test, no WSJ attribution, no IMO action).
